name: Camelopardalis
introduction: is the Giraffe, introduced by Petrus Plancius in 1612. It is a large but faint constellation near the north celestial pole.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: [Alpha Camelopardalis](hip:22783) is a runaway supergiant thousands of light-years away, moving so fast that it creates a bow shock in the surrounding gas.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Gamma Camelopardalis](hip:17959) is a white star, and [HD 21291](hip:16228) a supergiant.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: Camelopardalis contains Kemble’s Cascade, a chain of stars, the galaxy NGC 2403, and IC 342, the “Hidden Galaxy” behind the Milky Way’s dust. In 2014, the Camelopardalid meteor shower was observed.
